editorial:
Imagine you are stepping into a weird, dreamy version of suburban Italy where things feel slightly off. You follow a family that is just trying to keep their heads above water while dealing with the boring and painful parts of everyday life. The whole story revolves around a rugby game, but it is not really about the sport. It is more about how these people feel stuck and how they fight through their problems. The vibe is very slow and artistic, making you feel like you are watching a moving painting rather than a standard plot-driven movie.

You will notice that the acting is top-notch and the shots are gorgeous to look at, but be warned that the pace is very steady. If you like movies that make you think and feel rather than give you a fast story, you will love this. It is a bit strange, but that is what makes it special.
endingExplained: The movie ends by blurring the line between the rugby game and real life. You see that the struggle on the field was actually a way for the family to process their own pain and failures. There is no big victory or happy ending, but instead, a feeling of acceptance. The final scenes show the characters facing their reality, realizing that life is a long, slow game that you just have to keep playing.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves slow cinema and beautiful visuals.
